10	#

14	#   - rrid: Research Resource Identifier

17	#   - keywords: Search keywords (list)
18	#   - download_url: Download URL

20	#   - distribution_formats: DistributionFormat (list)
21	#

24	#   - ip_restrictions: IPRestrictions class

26	#   - confidentiality_level: ConfidentialityLevelEnum
27	#
28	# Human Subjects:
29	#   - human_subject_research: HumanSubjectResearch class
30	#   - informed_consent: InformedConsent (list)
31	#   - participant_privacy: ParticipantPrivacy (list)

33	#   - vulnerable_populations: VulnerablePopulations class
34	#   - ethical_reviews: EthicalReview (list)
35	#
36	# Data Composition:

38	#   - variables: VariableMetadata (list)
39	#   - subpopulations: Subpopulation (list)

43	# Data Quality:

53	#
54	# Hierarchical Structure:
55	#   - resources: Dataset (list) - nested sub-resources
56	#   - parent_datasets: Dataset (list) - parent datasets
57	#   - related_datasets: DatasetRelationship (list) - typed relationships
58	#
59	# Funding & Motivation:
60	#   - purposes: Purpose (list)
61	#   - tasks: Task (list)
62	#   - funders: FundingMechanism (list)
63	#   - creators: Creator (list)
64	#
65	# Technical Methods:
66	#   - collection_mechanisms: CollectionMechanism (list)
67	#   - acquisition_methods: DataAcquisition (list)
68	#   - preprocessing_strategies: PreprocessingStrategy (list)
69	#   - cleaning_strategies: CleaningStrategy (list)
70	#   - labeling_strategies: LabelingStrategy (list)
71	#   - software_and_tools: Software (list)
72	#

74	#   - version: Version string
75	#   - version_access: VersionAccess class
76	#   - updates: UpdatePlan class
77	#   - errata: Erratum (list)
78	#   - maintainers: Maintainer (list)
79	#   - was_derived_from: Source provenance
80	#   - release_notes: Release documentation
81	#
82	# Distribution:
83	#   - format: File format specification
84	#   - media_type: MIME type
85	#   - encoding: Character encoding

95	#   - content_warnings: Content warnings

98	#   - data_protection_impacts: DataProtectionImpact (list)
99	#   - reidentification_risk: Re-identification risk assessment

141	d4d_complex_proxy_rubric:
142	  schema_version: "2.0"
143	  description: >
144	    Ten-element hierarchical rubric for evaluating D4D YAML completeness and usability.
145	    Each element represents a complex metadata-driven goal and includes up to five measurable
146	    sub-elements. Scores can be computed at the element or sub-element level.
147	
148	  scoring_scale:
149	    element: 0–5
150	    sub_element: [0, 1]  # 0 = not present/fail, 1 = present/pass
151	
152	  rubric:
153	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
154	    - id: 1
155	      name: "Dataset Discovery and Identification"
156	      description: "Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?"
157	      sub_elements:
158	        - name: "Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)"
159	          field: ["doi", "rrid", "id"]
160	        - name: "Dataset Title and Description Completeness"
161	          field: ["title", "description"]
162	        - name: "Keywords or Tags for Searchability"
163	          field: ["keywords"]
164	        - name: "Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)"
165	          field: ["page", "resources"]
166	        - name: "Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)"
167	          field: ["parent_datasets", "related_datasets"]
168	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
169	
170	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
171	    - id: 2
172	      name: "Dataset Access and Retrieval"
173	      description: "Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?"
174	      sub_elements:
175	        - name: "Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined"
176	          field: ["license_and_use_terms", "ip_restrictions"]
177	        - name: "Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification"
178	          field: ["regulatory_restrictions", "confidentiality_level", "hipaa_compliant", "other_compliance", "governance_committee_contact"]
179	        - name: "Download URL or Platform Link Available"
180	          field: ["download_url"]
181	        - name: "Distribution Formats and File Types Specified"
182	          field: ["distribution_formats", "format", "media_type"]
183	        - name: "Related Datasets and External Resources Linked"
184	          field: ["related_datasets", "external_resources"]
185	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
186	
187	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
188	    - id: 3
189	      name: "Data Reuse and Interoperability"
190	      description: >
191	        Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?
192	
193	        Note: Evaluate whether the dataset is designed for integration with similar datasets,
194	        including: common identifiers for cross-dataset linking, standardized formats for data
195	        harmonization, and documented integration procedures.
196	      sub_elements:
197	        - name: "License Terms Allow Reuse"
198	          field: ["license_and_use_terms"]
199	        - name: "Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)"
200	          field: ["format", "encoding"]
201	        - name: "Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated"
202	          field: ["conforms_to", "conforms_to_schema"]
203	        - name: "Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined"
204	          field: ["variables"]
205	        - name: "Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)"
206	          field: ["intended_uses", "prohibited_uses", "discouraged_uses"]
207	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
208	
209	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
210	    - id: 4
211	      name: "Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards"
212	      description: "Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?"
213	      sub_elements:
214	        - name: "IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact"
215	          field: ["ethical_reviews", "human_subject_research", "data_protection_impacts"]
216	        - name: "Deidentification Method Described"
217	          field: ["is_deidentified"]
218	        - name: "Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment"
219	          field: ["participant_privacy", "reidentification_risk"]
220	        - name: "Informed Consent Obtained from Participants"
221	          field: ["informed_consent"]
222	        - name: "Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented"
223	          field: ["vulnerable_populations", "participant_compensation"]
224	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
225	
226	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
227	    - id: 5
228	      name: "Data Composition and Structure"
229	      description: "Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?"
230	      sub_elements:
231	        - name: "Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described"
232	          field: ["subpopulations"]
233	        - name: "Number of Instances or Samples Reported"
234	          field: ["instances"]
235	        - name: "Variable-Level Metadata, Tabular Flag, and Data Splits"
236	          field: ["variables", "is_tabular", "is_data_split", "is_subpopulation"]
237	        - name: "Data Topics or Conditions Represented"
238	          field: ["instances"]
239	        - name: "Data Quality, Anomalies, and Missing Data Documented"
240	          field: ["anomalies", "sampling_strategies", "missing_data_documentation"]
241	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
242	
243	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
244	    - id: 6
245	      name: "Data Provenance and Version Tracking"
246	      description: "Can a user determine dataset versions, update history, and provenance?"
247	      sub_elements:
248	        - name: "Dataset Version Number Provided"
249	          field: ["version"]
250	        - name: "Version Access Methods Documented"
251	          field: ["version_access"]
252	        - name: "Change Descriptions and Errata Provided"
253	          field: ["errata", "updates"]
254	        - name: "Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated"
255	          field: ["updates"]
256	        - name: "Provenance, Source Derivation, and Raw Data Sources"
257	          field: ["was_derived_from", "release_notes", "raw_data_sources"]
258	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
259	
260	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
261	    - id: 7
262	      name: "Scientific Motivation and Funding Transparency"
263	      description: "Does the metadata clearly state why the dataset exists and who funded it?"
264	      sub_elements:
265	        - name: "Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation"
266	          field: ["purposes"]
267	        - name: "Primary Research Objectives or Tasks"
268	          field: ["tasks"]
269	        - name: "Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed"
270	          field: ["funders"]
271	        - name: "Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present"
272	          field: ["funders"]
273	        - name: "Creators and Acknowledgements Documented"
274	          field: ["creators", "funders"]
275	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
276	
277	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
278	    - id: 8
279	      name: "Technical Transparency (Data Collection and Processing)"
280	      description: >
281	        Can data collection and processing steps be replicated or understood?
282	
283	        Note: Preprocessing and collection metadata may be represented as structured text
284	        descriptions OR as machine-readable provenance graphs (e.g., W3C PROV-O, workflow graphs).
285	        Evaluation should check for: (1) structured text descriptions OR (2) graph representations
286	        with entity-activity-agent relationships. Both formats are acceptable.
287	      sub_elements:
288	        - name: "Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described"
289	          field: ["collection_mechanisms"]
290	        - name: "Data Acquisition Methods Listed"
291	          field: ["acquisition_methods"]
292	        - name: "Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality"
293	          field: ["preprocessing_strategies", "cleaning_strategies", "labeling_strategies", "annotation_analyses", "machine_annotation_tools"]
294	        - name: "Software and Tools Documented"
295	          field: ["software_and_tools"]
296	        - name: "External Standards, Resources, and Imputation Protocols"
297	          field: ["external_resources", "conforms_to", "imputation_protocols"]
298	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
299	
300	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
301	    - id: 9
302	      name: "Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure"
303	      description: "Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?"
304	      sub_elements:
305	        - name: "Known Limitations Documented"
306	          field: ["known_limitations"]
307	        - name: "Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)"
308	          field: ["known_biases"]
309	        - name: "Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted"
310	          field: ["anomalies"]
311	        - name: "Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided"
312	          field: ["sensitive_elements", "content_warnings"]
313	        - name: "Ethical Review and Social Impact Analysis"
314	          field: ["ethical_reviews", "future_use_impacts"]
315	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
316	
317	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
318	    - id: 10
319	      name: "Cross-Platform and Community Integration"
320	      description: >
321	        Does the dataset connect to wider data ecosystems, repositories, or standards?
322	
323	        Note: For Bridge2AI datasets, citation metadata is mandatory and should include:
324	        (1) formatted citation string, (2) DOI, and (3) citation instructions. Hosting
325	        platform identification should specify the publisher or repository (e.g., PhysioNet,
326	        Dataverse, institutional repositories).
327	      sub_elements:
328	        - name: "Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform"
329	          field: ["publisher"]
330	        - name: "Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing"
331	          field: ["citation", "doi"]
332	        - name: "Community Standards or Schema Conformance"
333	          field: ["conforms_to"]
334	        - name: "Outreach Materials and Documentation Links"
335	          field: ["external_resources", "page"]
336	        - name: "Related Datasets with Typed Relationships"
337	          field: ["related_datasets"]
338	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
339

  schema_version: "2.0"
  description: >
    Ten-element hierarchical rubric for evaluating D4D YAML completeness and usability.
    Each element represents a complex metadata-driven goal and includes up to five measurable
    sub-elements. Scores can be computed at the element or sub-element level.

  scoring_scale:
    element: 0–5
    sub_element: [0, 1]  # 0 = not present/fail, 1 = present/pass

  rubric:
    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 1
      name: "Dataset Discovery and Identification"
      description: "Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?"
      sub_elements:
        - name: "Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)"
          field: ["doi", "rrid", "id"]
        - name: "Dataset Title and Description Completeness"
          field: ["title", "description"]
        - name: "Keywords or Tags for Searchability"
          field: ["keywords"]
        - name: "Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)"
          field: ["page", "resources"]
        - name: "Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)"
          field: ["parent_datasets", "related_datasets"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 2
      name: "Dataset Access and Retrieval"
      description: "Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?"
      sub_elements:
        - name: "Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined"
          field: ["license_and_use_terms", "ip_restrictions"]
        - name: "Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification"
          field: ["regulatory_restrictions", "confidentiality_level", "hipaa_compliant", "other_compliance", "governance_committee_contact"]
        - name: "Download URL or Platform Link Available"
          field: ["download_url"]
        - name: "Distribution Formats and File Types Specified"
          field: ["distribution_formats", "format", "media_type"]
        - name: "Related Datasets and External Resources Linked"
          field: ["related_datasets", "external_resources"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 3
      name: "Data Reuse and Interoperability"
      description: >
        Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?

        Note: Evaluate whether the dataset is designed for integration with similar datasets,
        including: common identifiers for cross-dataset linking, standardized formats for data
        harmonization, and documented integration procedures.
      sub_elements:
        - name: "License Terms Allow Reuse"
          field: ["license_and_use_terms"]
        - name: "Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)"
          field: ["format", "encoding"]
        - name: "Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated"
          field: ["conforms_to", "conforms_to_schema"]
        - name: "Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined"
          field: ["variables"]
        - name: "Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)"
          field: ["intended_uses", "prohibited_uses", "discouraged_uses"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 4
      name: "Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards"
      description: "Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?"
      sub_elements:
        - name: "IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact"
          field: ["ethical_reviews", "human_subject_research", "data_protection_impacts"]
        - name: "Deidentification Method Described"
          field: ["is_deidentified"]
        - name: "Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment"
          field: ["participant_privacy", "reidentification_risk"]
        - name: "Informed Consent Obtained from Participants"
          field: ["informed_consent"]
        - name: "Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented"
          field: ["vulnerable_populations", "participant_compensation"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 5
      name: "Data Composition and Structure"
      description: "Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?"
      sub_elements:
        - name: "Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described"
          field: ["subpopulations"]
        - name: "Number of Instances or Samples Reported"
          field: ["instances"]
        - name: "Variable-Level Metadata, Tabular Flag, and Data Splits"
          field: ["variables", "is_tabular", "is_data_split", "is_subpopulation"]
        - name: "Data Topics or Conditions Represented"
          field: ["instances"]
        - name: "Data Quality, Anomalies, and Missing Data Documented"
          field: ["anomalies", "sampling_strategies", "missing_data_documentation"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 6
      name: "Data Provenance and Version Tracking"
      description: "Can a user determine dataset versions, update history, and provenance?"
      sub_elements:
        - name: "Dataset Version Number Provided"
          field: ["version"]
        - name: "Version Access Methods Documented"
          field: ["version_access"]
        - name: "Change Descriptions and Errata Provided"
          field: ["errata", "updates"]
        - name: "Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated"
          field: ["updates"]
        - name: "Provenance, Source Derivation, and Raw Data Sources"
          field: ["was_derived_from", "release_notes", "raw_data_sources"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 7
      name: "Scientific Motivation and Funding Transparency"
      description: "Does the metadata clearly state why the dataset exists and who funded it?"
      sub_elements:
        - name: "Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation"
          field: ["purposes"]
        - name: "Primary Research Objectives or Tasks"
          field: ["tasks"]
        - name: "Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed"
          field: ["funders"]
        - name: "Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present"
          field: ["funders"]
        - name: "Creators and Acknowledgements Documented"
          field: ["creators", "funders"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 8
      name: "Technical Transparency (Data Collection and Processing)"
      description: >
        Can data collection and processing steps be replicated or understood?

        Note: Preprocessing and collection metadata may be represented as structured text
        descriptions OR as machine-readable provenance graphs (e.g., W3C PROV-O, workflow graphs).
        Evaluation should check for: (1) structured text descriptions OR (2) graph representations
        with entity-activity-agent relationships. Both formats are acceptable.
      sub_elements:
        - name: "Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described"
          field: ["collection_mechanisms"]
        - name: "Data Acquisition Methods Listed"
          field: ["acquisition_methods"]
        - name: "Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality"
          field: ["preprocessing_strategies", "cleaning_strategies", "labeling_strategies", "annotation_analyses", "machine_annotation_tools"]
        - name: "Software and Tools Documented"
          field: ["software_and_tools"]
        - name: "External Standards, Resources, and Imputation Protocols"
          field: ["external_resources", "conforms_to", "imputation_protocols"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 9
      name: "Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure"
      description: "Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?"
      sub_elements:
        - name: "Known Limitations Documented"
          field: ["known_limitations"]
        - name: "Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)"
          field: ["known_biases"]
        - name: "Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted"
          field: ["anomalies"]
        - name: "Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided"
          field: ["sensitive_elements", "content_warnings"]
        - name: "Ethical Review and Social Impact Analysis"
          field: ["ethical_reviews", "future_use_impacts"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 10
      name: "Cross-Platform and Community Integration"
      description: >
        Does the dataset connect to wider data ecosystems, repositories, or standards?

        Note: For Bridge2AI datasets, citation metadata is mandatory and should include:
        (1) formatted citation string, (2) DOI, and (3) citation instructions. Hosting
        platform identification should specify the publisher or repository (e.g., PhysioNet,
        Dataverse, institutional repositories).
      sub_elements:
        - name: "Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform"
          field: ["publisher"]
        - name: "Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing"
          field: ["citation", "doi"]
        - name: "Community Standards or Schema Conformance"
          field: ["conforms_to"]
        - name: "Outreach Materials and Documentation Links"
          field: ["external_resources", "page"]
        - name: "Related Datasets with Typed Relationships"
          field: ["related_datasets"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

16	id: https://chorus4ai.org/#dataset
17	name: CHoRUS Dataset
18	title: "Bridge2AI: Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for Equitable AI"
19	description: >-
20	  The CHoRUS dataset is a multicenter, multimodal, high-resolution, controlled-access dataset of
21	  acute and critical care hospital admissions, assembled retrospectively by the CHoRUS Network, one
22	  of four data generation projects in the NIH Common Fund's Bridge2AI program. Data are contributed
23	  by 14 data acquisition hospitals among the 20 academic centers in the collaboration, whose
24	  membership is given as more than 60 consortium members. Structured electronic health record data
25	  are standardized to the OMOP Common Data Model; unstructured EHR text is extracted and tokenized
26	  with the OHNLP toolkit; imaging is drawn from hospital PACS in DICOM; telemetry waveforms from
27	  bedside monitors and gateway/middleware are released in WFDB; and EEG waveforms from hospital EEG
28	  databases are released in EDF+ and Persyst formats. Social determinants of health and contextual
29	  factors such as geographic distance to the nearest hospital are also acquired. The project website
30	  reports a current released dataset of 50,000 patient admissions from ICU, PICU, and NICU settings,
31	  1.6 billion rows of EHR OMOP data, 7,642 admissions with radiology data, and 23 Tb of waveform
32	  data, against an anticipated final dataset of 100,000 patient admissions covering 9 data
33	  modalities from 14 contributing hospitals. The nine documented data types are demographics,
34	  medication administration, procedures, nursing flowsheets, diagnoses, clinical notes, imaging,
35	  waveform telemetry, and EEG waveform; every one of them is under controlled access. OMOP and
36	  telemetry data sit in a cloud enclave, clinical notes remain stored locally at contributing sites
37	  with only tokens centralized, and as of August 2025 imaging de-identification for a larger cohort
38	  and EEG extraction were still in process. The project also sequesters a holdout test set for
39	  external validation of models.
40	status: partially released
41	page: https://chorus4ai.org/
42	created_by: CHoRUS Consortium
43	is_tabular: false

45	- critical care

47	- critical illness
48	- electronic health record
49	- OMOP Common Data Model
50	- waveform telemetry

52	- imaging

54	- social determinants of health
55	- multimodality
56	- AI-ready data set
57	- Bridge2AI
58	conforms_to: >-
59	  Structured EHR data conform to the OMOP Common Data Model (with extensions for nursing flowsheets);
60	  imaging conforms to DICOM; waveform telemetry conforms to WFDB, described in the source as a
61	  PhysioNet schema extended; EEG conforms to EDF+ and Persyst; tokenized clinical notes conform to
62	  the OHNLP open source schema.
63	conforms_to_standard:
64	- OMOP_CDM
65	- DICOM
66	- WFDB
67	- OTHER
68	conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema
69	conforms_to_class: Dataset
70	notes: >-
71	  The project website carries a site-wide banner reading "This repoitory is under review for
72	  potential modification in compliance with Administration directives." The misspelling of
73	  "repository" is reproduced as published. The same website carries the funding statement "This
74	  project is funded by the NIH under award number OT2OD032701. The content on this website is solely
75	  the responsibility of the authors and does not necessarily represent the official views of the
76	  NIH."
77	source_caveats: >-
78	  The two sources that quantify the dataset disagree. The tier-2 project documentation
79	  (chorus4ai.org) states a current released dataset of 50,000 patient admissions and 7,642
80	  admissions with radiology data; the tier-4 cohort_2_webinar states that "As of August 2025, covers
81	  14 different hospitals with over 45K unique admissions" and that 1000 images are currently
82	  available. The tier-2 values are stated in this record, with the webinar's August 2025 snapshot
83	  reported where it describes modality readiness; the conflict is also recorded on the individual
84	  values it affects. The two imaging figures are expressed in different units (images versus
85	  admissions with radiology data) and may not be directly comparable. A single OTHER term in
86	  conforms_to_standard stands for three distinct standards the registered enum does not cover: EDF+,
87	  Persyst, and the OHNLP open source schema. The WFDB entry likewise covers a schema the source
88	  describes as extended rather than plain WFDB. The bundle gives no release date, DOI, version
89	  identifier, or recommended citation for the dataset, and does not state the language of the
90	  dataset content.

141	purposes:
142	- response: >-
143	    Meet the need of generating data for ML/AI applications aimed at characterizing acute and
144	    critical care illness, predicting complications, and measuring treatment response among patients
145	    with acute or critical illness.
146	- response: >-
147	    Develop a publicly available, AI-ready critical care dataset while ensuring the methods promote
148	    privacy, accountability, and clinical benefit, and while promoting a new generation of AI
149	    clinicians and scientists.
150	- response: >-
151	    Develop the most diverse, high-resolution, ethically sourced, AI-ready data set to answer the
152	    grand challenge of improving recovery from acute illness.
153	- response: >-
154	    Create ethically sourced datasets and tools around artificial intelligence and create best
155	    practices for AI in health, as one of four data generation projects in the NIH Bridge2AI
156	    consortium.

158	addressing_gaps:
159	- response: >-
160	    There is an urgent need for infrastructure to support artificial intelligence and machine
161	    learning in critical care; developing high-resolution multi-center data sets is a critical first
162	    step towards actionable and trustworthy AI.
163	- response: >-
164	    Existing critical care data lack the diversity and resolution needed for AI; the project acquires
165	    and standardizes a dataset of unprecedented diversity and high resolution across a multi-center
166	    network.
167	- response: >-
168	    Multi-modal EHR, waveform, imaging, and text data are not harmonized; unified standards and
169	    validated semantic mappings are developed to make them interoperable.

172	- response: Characterizing acute and critical care illness.
173	- response: Predicting complications and clinical deterioration among patients with acute or critical illness.
174	- response: Measuring treatment response among patients with acute or critical illness.
175	- response: >-
176	    External validation of AI/ML models against a sequestered holdout test set, to aid marketplace
177	    adoption of AI-developed models for implementation in acute and critical care.
178	- response: >-
179	    Labeling data with targets important for prediction using a visualization and annotation
180	    environment.

185	    The dataset is intended to support building ML- and AI-derived models to improve the care and
186	    outcomes of patients requiring critical care.

189	  - Measurement of treatment response in acute and critical illness
190	- use_category: External validation of AI models
191	  usage_notes: >-
192	    A holdout test set is provisioned specifically for external validation of models developed
193	    elsewhere.
194	- use_category: Training and workforce development in clinical AI
195	  usage_notes: >-
196	    The dataset is used within the Bridge2AI AI/ML for Clinical Care Collaborative Cloud for
197	    hands-on AI/ML coursework, canonical Jupyter Notebooks, and OHDSI/OMOP instruction, including
198	    trainee development of use cases and works-in-progress posters, conference abstracts, and
199	    manuscripts.

219	    Retrospective extraction of structured electronic health record data (demographics, medication
220	    administration with dosing time-stamped upon each infusion change or dose administration,
221	    procedures documented by providers, high-frequency nursing flowsheet documentation, and
222	    provider-documented diagnoses) from contributing hospital systems, standardized to the OMOP
223	    Common Data Model.
224	- was_directly_observed: true

226	    Waveform telemetry captured from bedside monitors through hospital gateway/middleware and
227	    delivered in WFDB format.
228	- was_directly_observed: true
229	  acquisition_details: Imaging studies retrieved from hospital PACS in DICOM format.
230	- was_directly_observed: true

232	    EEG waveforms extracted from hospital EEG databases in EDF+ and Persyst formats; extraction was

243	- mechanism_details: Hospital picture archiving and communication systems (PACS) supply imaging.
244	- mechanism_details: Hospital EEG databases supply EEG waveform recordings.
245	- mechanism_details: >-
246	    The OHNLP toolkit is used to extract and tokenize unstructured clinical notes.
247	- mechanism_details: >-

336	- bias_type: representation_bias
337	  bias_description: >-
338	    The project treats cohort balance and diversity as an open risk to be managed: patient-focused
339	    efforts determine the ethical and legal approaches to manage privacy and bias while accounting
340	    for social determinants of health, and the stated goal is the most diverse AI-ready data set for
341	    improving recovery from acute illness.
342	  mitigation_strategy: >-
343	    Federated access will enable sampling methods to ensure a balanced and diverse cohort, and
344	    sampling at scale is designed to capture comprehensive sets of patient conditions and clinical
345	    treatment strategies.

# D4D Datasheet for CHORUS Dataset
# Generation Method: schema-grounded agentic, phase 1
# Agent runtime: Claude API (direct)
# Provider: LBL CBORG (proxy to Anthropic)
# Model: claude-opus-5
# Mode: four-phase project agent, generic-v7 prompt
# Prompt: src/download/prompts/d4d_generic_arm_prompt_v7.md (identical for all projects)
# Arm: BASELINE (input documents only)
# Source bundle: data/preprocessed/concatenated/CHORUS_preprocessed.txt
# Source manifest: data/preprocessed/source_manifest.yaml
# Schema: src/data_sheets_schema/schema/data_sheets_schema_all.yaml
# Prior D4D factual reuse: prohibited
# Temperature: 0.0
# Generated: 2026-09-02

id: https://chorus4ai.org/#dataset
name: CHoRUS Dataset
title: "Bridge2AI: Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for Equitable AI"
description: >-
  The CHoRUS dataset is a multicenter, multimodal, high-resolution, controlled-access dataset of
  acute and critical care hospital admissions, assembled retrospectively by the CHoRUS Network, one
  of four data generation projects in the NIH Common Fund's Bridge2AI program. Data are contributed
  by 14 data acquisition hospitals among the 20 academic centers in the collaboration, whose
  membership is given as more than 60 consortium members. Structured electronic health record data
  are standardized to the OMOP Common Data Model; unstructured EHR text is extracted and tokenized
  with the OHNLP toolkit; imaging is drawn from hospital PACS in DICOM; telemetry waveforms from
  bedside monitors and gateway/middleware are released in WFDB; and EEG waveforms from hospital EEG
  databases are released in EDF+ and Persyst formats. Social determinants of health and contextual
  factors such as geographic distance to the nearest hospital are also acquired. The project website
  reports a current released dataset of 50,000 patient admissions from ICU, PICU, and NICU settings,
  1.6 billion rows of EHR OMOP data, 7,642 admissions with radiology data, and 23 Tb of waveform
  data, against an anticipated final dataset of 100,000 patient admissions covering 9 data
  modalities from 14 contributing hospitals. The nine documented data types are demographics,
  medication administration, procedures, nursing flowsheets, diagnoses, clinical notes, imaging,
  waveform telemetry, and EEG waveform; every one of them is under controlled access. OMOP and
  telemetry data sit in a cloud enclave, clinical notes remain stored locally at contributing sites
  with only tokens centralized, and as of August 2025 imaging de-identification for a larger cohort
  and EEG extraction were still in process. The project also sequesters a holdout test set for
  external validation of models.
status: partially released
page: https://chorus4ai.org/
created_by: CHoRUS Consortium
is_tabular: false
keywords:
- critical care
- acute illness
- critical illness
- electronic health record
- OMOP Common Data Model
- waveform telemetry
- electroencephalography
- imaging
- clinical notes
- social determinants of health
- multimodality
- AI-ready data set
- Bridge2AI
conforms_to: >-
  Structured EHR data conform to the OMOP Common Data Model (with extensions for nursing flowsheets);
  imaging conforms to DICOM; waveform telemetry conforms to WFDB, described in the source as a
  PhysioNet schema extended; EEG conforms to EDF+ and Persyst; tokenized clinical notes conform to
  the OHNLP open source schema.
conforms_to_standard:
- OMOP_CDM
- DICOM
- WFDB
- OTHER
conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema
conforms_to_class: Dataset
notes: >-
  The project website carries a site-wide banner reading "This repoitory is under review for
  potential modification in compliance with Administration directives." The misspelling of
  "repository" is reproduced as published. The same website carries the funding statement "This
  project is funded by the NIH under award number OT2OD032701. The content on this website is solely
  the responsibility of the authors and does not necessarily represent the official views of the
  NIH."
source_caveats: >-
  The two sources that quantify the dataset disagree. The tier-2 project documentation
  (chorus4ai.org) states a current released dataset of 50,000 patient admissions and 7,642
  admissions with radiology data; the tier-4 cohort_2_webinar states that "As of August 2025, covers
  14 different hospitals with over 45K unique admissions" and that 1000 images are currently
  available. The tier-2 values are stated in this record, with the webinar's August 2025 snapshot
  reported where it describes modality readiness; the conflict is also recorded on the individual
  values it affects. The two imaging figures are expressed in different units (images versus
  admissions with radiology data) and may not be directly comparable. A single OTHER term in
  conforms_to_standard stands for three distinct standards the registered enum does not cover: EDF+,
  Persyst, and the OHNLP open source schema. The WFDB entry likewise covers a schema the source
  describes as extended rather than plain WFDB. The bundle gives no release date, DOI, version
  identifier, or recommended citation for the dataset, and does not state the language of the
  dataset content.

purposes:
- response: >-
    Meet the need of generating data for ML/AI applications aimed at characterizing acute and
    critical care illness, predicting complications, and measuring treatment response among patients
    with acute or critical illness.
- response: >-
    Develop a publicly available, AI-ready critical care dataset while ensuring the methods promote
    privacy, accountability, and clinical benefit, and while promoting a new generation of AI
    clinicians and scientists.
- response: >-
    Develop the most diverse, high-resolution, ethically sourced, AI-ready data set to answer the
    grand challenge of improving recovery from acute illness.
- response: >-
    Create ethically sourced datasets and tools around artificial intelligence and create best
    practices for AI in health, as one of four data generation projects in the NIH Bridge2AI
    consortium.

addressing_gaps:
- response: >-
    There is an urgent need for infrastructure to support artificial intelligence and machine
    learning in critical care; developing high-resolution multi-center data sets is a critical first
    step towards actionable and trustworthy AI.
- response: >-
    Existing critical care data lack the diversity and resolution needed for AI; the project acquires
    and standardizes a dataset of unprecedented diversity and high resolution across a multi-center
    network.
- response: >-
    Multi-modal EHR, waveform, imaging, and text data are not harmonized; unified standards and
    validated semantic mappings are developed to make them interoperable.

tasks:
- response: Characterizing acute and critical care illness.
- response: Predicting complications and clinical deterioration among patients with acute or critical illness.
- response: Measuring treatment response among patients with acute or critical illness.
- response: >-
    External validation of AI/ML models against a sequestered holdout test set, to aid marketplace
    adoption of AI-developed models for implementation in acute and critical care.
- response: >-
    Labeling data with targets important for prediction using a visualization and annotation
    environment.

intended_uses:
- use_category: Machine learning and artificial intelligence model development for acute and critical care
  usage_notes: >-
    The dataset is intended to support building ML- and AI-derived models to improve the care and
    outcomes of patients requiring critical care.
  examples:
  - Prediction of complications and deterioration in critically ill patients
  - Measurement of treatment response in acute and critical illness
- use_category: External validation of AI models
  usage_notes: >-
    A holdout test set is provisioned specifically for external validation of models developed
    elsewhere.
- use_category: Training and workforce development in clinical AI
  usage_notes: >-
    The dataset is used within the Bridge2AI AI/ML for Clinical Care Collaborative Cloud for
    hands-on AI/ML coursework, canonical Jupyter Notebooks, and OHDSI/OMOP instruction, including
    trainee development of use cases and works-in-progress posters, conference abstracts, and
    manuscripts.

existing_uses:
- examples:
  - "Datasets are being used for training activities and publications"
- examples:
  - >-
      The AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for Clinical Care Training Program (Cohort 2) expands access to
      Bridge2AI CHoRUS data so that up to 30 trainees can apply AI/ML methods to big data analysis
      and conduct research on the Bridge2AI Clinical Care Cloud platform

future_use_impacts:
- impact_details: >-
    The project sequesters holdout datasets for external validation in order to aid marketplace
    adoption of AI-developed models for implementation in acute and critical care, and to catalyze
    the biomedical research and expertise necessary to promote the patient-focused deployment of AI.

acquisition_methods:
- was_directly_observed: true
  acquisition_details: >-
    Retrospective extraction of structured electronic health record data (demographics, medication
    administration with dosing time-stamped upon each infusion change or dose administration,
    procedures documented by providers, high-frequency nursing flowsheet documentation, and
    provider-documented diagnoses) from contributing hospital systems, standardized to the OMOP
    Common Data Model.
- was_directly_observed: true
  acquisition_details: >-
    Waveform telemetry captured from bedside monitors through hospital gateway/middleware and
    delivered in WFDB format.
- was_directly_observed: true
  acquisition_details: Imaging studies retrieved from hospital PACS in DICOM format.
- was_directly_observed: true
  acquisition_details: >-
    EEG waveforms extracted from hospital EEG databases in EDF+ and Persyst formats; extraction was
    still in process as of August 2025.
- was_directly_observed: true
  acquisition_details: >-
    Clinical notes documented by providers are extracted from hospital systems and tokenized using
    the OHNLP toolkit; the notes themselves are stored locally at contributing sites and only tokens
    are centralized.

collection_mechanisms:
- mechanism_details: >-
    Bedside physiologic monitors together with hospital gateway/middleware supply waveform telemetry.
- mechanism_details: Hospital picture archiving and communication systems (PACS) supply imaging.
- mechanism_details: Hospital EEG databases supply EEG waveform recordings.
- mechanism_details: >-
    The OHNLP toolkit is used to extract and tokenize unstructured clinical notes.
- mechanism_details: >-
    The chorus-extract-upload Python tool in the chorus-ai GitHub organization provides tools to
    create and upload a CHoRUS Data Extract at contributing sites.

data_collectors:
- collector_details: >-
    Fourteen of the twenty academic centers in the CHoRUS collaboration contribute as Data
    Acquisition centers, extracting and delivering clinical data extracts to the project.
- collector_details: >-
    Data site managers at contributing sites follow an interactive workflow and step-by-step standard
    operating procedures published in the Chorus_SOP repository, which have undergone an internal
    validation and review process, and report progress through GitHub or a Google Form that updates
    the Standards Project and Data Acquisition Project boards.

direct_collection:
- is_direct: false
  collection_details: >-
    Data collection is retrospective: clinical data are extracted from hospital clinical systems
    (EHR, PACS, bedside monitors, EEG databases) at data contributing sites rather than gathered
    directly from patients for research purposes.

collection_timeframes:
- timeframe_details: >-
    Data collection is described as retrospective and is carried out over the NIH award period, which
    runs from 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30. As of August 2025 the assembled dataset covered 14 different
    hospitals.
  source_caveats: >-
    The dates given are the NIH project period for award OT2OD032701, not the clinical period the
    admissions are drawn from. Because extraction is retrospective, the admissions almost certainly
    predate the award, and the bundle does not state the temporal coverage of the clinical data.

sampling_strategies:
- is_sample: true
  strategies: >-
    Sampling at scale across data contributing centers to ensure comprehensive sets of patient
    conditions and clinical treatment strategies
- strategies: >-
    Federated access will enable sampling methods to ensure a balanced and diverse cohort

instances:
- instance_type: Patient admission from ICU, PICU, and NICU
  counts: 50000
  data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:4
  source_caveats: >-
    The tier-2 project documentation gives 50,000 patient admissions in the current released dataset;
    the tier-4 cohort 2 webinar states "over 45K unique admissions" as of August 2025. The tier-2
    figure is recorded here.
- instance_type: Row of EHR data in the OMOP Common Data Model
  counts: 1600000000
  data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:37
  data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:9
- instance_type: Admission with radiology data
  counts: 7642
  data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:11
  data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:15
  source_caveats: >-
    The tier-2 project documentation gives 7,642 admissions with radiology data in the current
    released dataset; the tier-4 cohort 2 webinar states that 1000 images were available as of August
    2025 with de-identification in process for a larger cohort. The two figures use different units
    and may not be directly comparable; the tier-2 figure is recorded here.
- instance_type: Waveform telemetry recording from bedside monitors
  data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:49
  data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:37
  notes: The current released dataset is reported as 23 Tb of waveform data.
- instance_type: EEG waveform recording from hospital EEG databases
  data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:49
  data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:37
- instance_type: Tokenized clinical note
  data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:43
  data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:32

subpopulations:
- subpopulation_elements_present: true
  identification: >-
    Admissions in the current release are drawn from adult intensive care (ICU), pediatric intensive
    care (PICU), and neonatal intensive care (NICU) settings.
- subpopulation_elements_present: true
  identification: >-
    Demographics are captured as one of the nine data modalities and standardized to the OMOP Common
    Data Model; social determinants of health and contextual factors such as geographic distance to
    the nearest hospital are acquired alongside them.

splits:
- split_details: >-
    The dataset provisions a holdout test set, sequestered from the released data and accessible for
    external validation of models, intended to aid marketplace adoption of AI-developed models for
    implementation in acute and critical care.

known_biases:
- bias_type: representation_bias
  bias_description: >-
    The project treats cohort balance and diversity as an open risk to be managed: patient-focused
    efforts determine the ethical and legal approaches to manage privacy and bias while accounting
    for social determinants of health, and the stated goal is the most diverse AI-ready data set for
    improving recovery from acute illness.
  mitigation_strategy: >-
    Federated access will enable sampling methods to ensure a balanced and diverse cohort, and
    sampling at scale is designed to capture comprehensive sets of patient conditions and clinical
    treatment strategies.

known_limitations:
- limitation_type: coverage_limitation
  limitation_description: >-
    Modality availability is uneven and still developing. As of August 2025 the cohort 2 webinar
    reported that 1000 images were available with de-identification in process for a larger imaging
    cohort, that EEG extraction was still in process, and that published metadata was only planned
    rather than available for clinical notes, imaging, and EEG. The project website separately
    reports 7,642 admissions with radiology data in the current released dataset.
  recommended_mitigation: >-
    Confirm current modality availability with the CHoRUS data access contacts before planning
    analyses that depend on imaging, EEG, or note tokens.
- limitation_type: scope_limitation
  limitation_description: >-
    The released dataset is a partial build: 50,000 patient admissions against an anticipated final
    dataset of 100,000 patient admissions.
- limitation_type: integration_limitation
  limitation_description: >-
    Clinical notes are not centralized with the rest of the data; they are stored locally at
    contributing sites and only tokens produced by the OHNLP toolkit are available in the enclave,
    which constrains analyses requiring raw narrative text.
- limitation_type: representativeness_limitation
  limitation_description: >-
    Data are contributed by 14 hospitals drawn from the 20 academic centers in the collaboration, so
    the cohort reflects the case mix and practice patterns of those participating academic centers.

preprocessing_strategies:
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Source clinical data are standardized to the OMOP Common Data Model, with schema extensions used
    for high-frequency nursing flowsheet documentation.
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Unstructured electronic health record text is extracted and tokenized using the OHNLP toolkit and
    represented in the OHNLP open source schema.
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Data are transformed using approaches that limit re-identification before release.
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Waveforms are prepared and converted using the waveform conversion scripts and documentation in
    the chorus_waveform and chorus_waveform_resources repositories, with telemetry released in WFDB
    (described as a PhysioNet schema extended) and EEG in EDF+ and Persyst.
- preprocessing_details: >-
    OMOP Location entities are geocoded via DeGauss using the open source UF-Geocoding code, a fork
    of bihorac-LAB/Exposome maintained in the chorus-ai GitHub organization.

cleaning_strategies:
- cleaning_details: >-
    Characterization reports are produced and returned to sites following their data submissions,
    using the CHoRUSReports repository, so that contributing sites can identify and resolve issues in
    their extracts.
- cleaning_details: >-
    Semantic mappings from source formats to international standards are validated; clinical
    collaborators contribute to pooled tabular mappings in the chorus-mapping repository under an
    associated clinical validation standard operating procedure.

labeling_strategies:
- labeling_details: >-
    A visualization and annotation environment is developed to label data with targets important for
    prediction, as part of the project's capability to acquire, standardize, tokenize, store,
    visualize, and label data across the multi-center network.

raw_data_sources:
- source_description: >-
    Structured electronic health record data from contributing hospital systems, covering
    demographics, medication administration, procedures, nursing flowsheets, and diagnoses
  source_type: Hospital electronic health record system
  raw_data_format: Site-specific source formats subsequently mapped to the OMOP Common Data Model
- source_description: Unstructured clinical notes documented in hospital electronic health record systems
  source_type: Hospital electronic health record system
  raw_data_format: Free text, extracted and tokenized with the OHNLP toolkit
  access_details: >-
    Notes are stored locally at the contributing site; only tokens are made available centrally.
- source_description: Imaging studies held in hospital picture archiving and communication systems
  source_type: Hospital PACS
  raw_data_format: DICOM
- source_description: Waveform telemetry from bedside monitors captured through gateway/middleware
  source_type: Bedside physiologic monitoring infrastructure
  raw_data_format: WFDB
- source_description: EEG recordings held in hospital EEG databases
  source_type: Hospital EEG database
  raw_data_format: EDF+ and Persyst
- source_description: >-
    Social determinants of health and contextual factors such as geographic distance to the nearest
    hospital
  source_type: Contextual and geospatial data linked to OMOP Location entities

distribution_formats:
- format: OMOP Common Data Model tables
  notes: >-
    Used for demographics, medication administration, procedures, nursing flowsheets, and diagnoses;
    the nursing flowsheet tables use the OMOP schema with extensions.
- format: OHNLP open source schema
  notes: Tokenized clinical notes.
- format: DICOM
  notes: Imaging extracted from PACS.
- format: WFDB
  notes: Waveform telemetry, described in the source as a PhysioNet schema extended.
- format: EDF+ and Persyst
  notes: EEG waveform recordings.

third_party_sharing:
- is_shared: true
  notes: >-
    The dataset is made available to users outside the contributing hospitals under controlled
    access, including trainees enrolled in the AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for Clinical Care Training
    Program, after a licensing agreement is signed.

data_governance:
  accountable_organization:
    name: Massachusetts General Hospital
  committee_contact: Jared Houghtaling
  access_review_process: >-
    All nine data modalities are under controlled access, and two distinct access routes are
    documented. General route: requests for access are directed to dbold@emory.edu or
    jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org. Training-program route: participants in the AIM-AHEAD
    Bridge2AI for Clinical Care Training Program complete a registration form with name, email, and
    institution and must sign a licensing agreement included in the registration form before gaining
    access to the dataset; once access is granted and compute is provisioned, an email is sent. A
    ".edu" email address is required in order to gain access to the dataset through that route,
    though program administrators will assist with this access if needed and the requirement is not a
    barrier to acceptance into the program.
  stewardship_roles:
  - >-
      Program Manager Ciera McCrary at Massachusetts General Hospital is the contact listed on the
      project website
  - >-
      Data access requests are handled by the CHoRUS contacts reachable at dbold@emory.edu and
      jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org
  - >-
      Data contributing sites are responsible for creating and curating their CHoRUS-specific
      clinical data extract and for providing regular status updates on that progress
  source_caveats: >-
    The bundle names no access committee, no committee membership, no decision timeframe, and no
    appeal process. Jared Houghtaling is recorded as the contact because the chorus-ai GitHub
    organization lists him as one of two addresses for requesting access; the bundle does not state
    that he chairs or sits on any access body.

license_and_use_terms:
  license_terms: >-
    Every data modality is released under controlled access rather than an open license. Users must
    sign a licensing agreement before gaining access to the dataset, and access through the AIM-AHEAD
    training program additionally requires a ".edu" email address.
  notes: >-
    The MIT License stated for the chorus-ai GitHub organization, and the Apache-2.0 license shown on
    some individual repositories such as Chorus_SOP, govern the CHoRUS software repositories and not
    the dataset itself.

regulatory_restrictions:
  confidentiality_level: restricted
  regulatory_restrictions:
  - >-
      Access to all data modalities is controlled and conditional on a signed licensing agreement
  - >-
      The project establishes a legal framework for collecting data at scale and analyzes the
      existing legal and regulatory landscape to manage privacy and bias

ethical_reviews:
- reviewing_organization: CHoRUS consortium
  review_details: >-
    The project performs community-facing ethics focus groups to determine what data is appropriate
    for public sharing, and evaluates community perspectives on clinical care AI to find ways to
    increase trustworthiness of provenance and privacy in AI. Ethics is one of the project's three
    pillars, described in the NIH abstract as "Ethics (Ethical and Trustworthy AI)".
  source_caveats: >-
    This describes ethics activity carried out by the consortium. The bundle names no IRB, ethics
    committee, or approval identifier, and does not state that any body performed a formal ethical
    review of the dataset.
- reviewing_organization: CHoRUS consortium
  review_details: >-
    Patient-focused efforts determine the ethical and legal approaches used to manage privacy and
    bias while accounting for social determinants of health; new approaches are created as the
    existing legal and regulatory landscape is analyzed.
  source_caveats: >-
    Recorded from the project website and GitHub organization README; no reviewing body is named in
    either source.

human_subject_research:
  involves_human_subjects: true
  special_populations:
  - >-
    The cohort consists of acutely and critically ill hospital patients, and the released admissions
    include pediatric intensive care (PICU) and neonatal intensive care (NICU) patients.
  source_caveats: >-
    The NIH abstract describes the project as addressing the challenges of acquiring an AI-ready data
    set from more than 100,000 critically ill patients, which is the anticipated scale rather than a
    count of data already collected. The bundle names no IRB, ethics review board, or approval
    number.

is_deidentified:
  method: >-
    Tokenization of unstructured electronic health record text using the OHNLP toolkit, retention of
    clinical notes at the local site with only tokens released, de-identification of imaging (in
    process for the larger cohort as of August 2025), and transformation of data using approaches
    that limit re-identification.
  deidentification_details: >-
    The project acquires, standardizes and tokenizes source clinical data and transforms it using
    approaches that limit re-identification before release into the controlled-access enclave. As of
    August 2025, 1000 images were available with de-identification in process for a larger imaging
    cohort.
  source_caveats: >-
    The bundle documents de-identification activity but does not state whether identifiable elements
    remain present in the released dataset, so that determination is left unrecorded.

participant_privacy:
- privacy_techniques: >-
    Tokenization of unstructured EHR text; Local retention of clinical notes at contributing sites,
    with only tokens centralized; A privacy scan tool for medical records, maintained in the
    privacy_scan_tool repository; A de-identification component maintained in the CTP-deid
    repository
  reidentification_risk: >-
    The project transforms data using approaches that limit re-identification, and patient-focused
    ethics and legal work determines the approaches used to manage privacy.
  source_caveats: >-
    The CTP-deid repository is listed in the chorus-ai GitHub organization without a description; the
    bundle does not expand the abbreviation or state what the component does beyond its name.

sensitive_elements:
- sensitive_elements_present: true
  sensitivity_details: >-
    The dataset comprises hospital clinical records of critically ill patients, including
    demographics, diagnoses, medication administration, procedures, nursing flowsheets, clinical
    note tokens, radiology images, telemetry and EEG waveforms, social determinants of health, and
    contextual geographic factors such as distance to the nearest hospital.

confidential_elements:
- confidential_elements_present: true
  confidentiality_details: >-
    All nine data modalities carry controlled access. Clinical notes cannot be released centrally and
    are stored locally at contributing sites, with only tokens made available in the enclave;
    community-facing ethics focus groups are used to determine what data is appropriate for public
    sharing.

maintainers:
- role: academic_institution
  maintainer_details: >-
    The CHoRUS consortium, coordinated from Massachusetts General Hospital, maintains the dataset;
    Ciera McCrary, MGH, Program Manager, is the contact listed on the project website
    (cmccrary@mgh.havard.edu).
  source_caveats: >-
    The email address is reproduced exactly as published on chorus4ai.org, where the domain appears
    as "mgh.havard.edu"; this looks like a typographical error in the source and was not corrected.
- role: academic_institution
  maintainer_details: >-
    Access requests are received by the CHoRUS contacts dbold@emory.edu and
    jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org.
- maintainer_details: >-
    Versions, maintainers, and other metadata about the CHoRUS software packages that support the
    dataset are tracked on the package status page compiled in the chorus-developer repository.

updates:
  update_details: >-
    The released dataset is being expanded toward an anticipated final dataset of 100,000 patient
    admissions covering 9 data modalities from 14 contributing hospitals. As of August 2025,
    de-identification of a larger imaging cohort and extraction of EEG waveforms were in process, and
    published metadata schemas were planned but not yet available for clinical notes, imaging, and
    EEG.

extension_mechanism:
  contribution_url: https://github.com/chorus-ai
  extension_details: >-
    Clinical collaborators can contribute to semantic mapping efforts through the chorus-mapping
    repository, which holds documentation and pooled tabular mappings together with a clinical
    validation standard operating procedure. Issues encountered in creating or submitting a data
    extract can be posted in the Standards Discussions or Data Acquisition Discussions areas of the
    chorus-ai GitHub organization, and data contributing sites submit status updates either through
    the GitHub interface or through a Google Form that triggers a GoogleScript calling the GitHub API
    to update status and issue information.

external_resources:
- external_resources:
  - >-
      https://chorus4ai.org/ - the public-facing CHoRUS project webpage, with pages on the team,
      project overview, tools, data acquisition, standards, community engagement, ethics, the
      dataset, and learning resources
  - >-
      https://github.com/chorus-ai - the CHoRUS GitHub organization, housing 28 repositories of
      software and tooling for clinical data, validated semantic mappings, standard operating
      protocols for data contributing sites, and project management overviews
  - >-
      https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10472824 - the NIH RePORTER record for award
      OT2OD032701
  - >-
      www.bridge2ai.org/chorus - the CHoRUS website given as a contact point in the chorus-ai GitHub
      organization README, recorded as written in the source, without a URL scheme

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""
3	Validate D4D evaluation JSON files against their schemas.
4	
5	This ensures evaluations conform to the standardized schema, which in turn
6	ensures HTML renderers can reliably parse the output.
7	"""
8	import argparse
9	import json
10	import re as _re
11	import sys
12	from pathlib import Path
13	from typing import Dict, List, Tuple
14	
15	try:
16	    import jsonschema
17	    from jsonschema import validate, ValidationError
18	except ImportError:
19	    print("ERROR: jsonschema package not installed")
20	    print("Install with: pip install jsonschema")
21	    sys.exit(1)
22	
23	
24	def load_schema(schema_path: Path) -> Dict:
25	    """Load JSON Schema file."""
26	    with open(schema_path, 'r') as f:
27	        return json.load(f)
28	
29	
30	def load_evaluation(eval_path: Path) -> Dict:
31	    """Load evaluation JSON file."""
32	    with open(eval_path, 'r') as f:
33	        return json.load(f)
34	
35	
36	#: Top-level keys of the shape that preceded the current agent contract.
37	#: rubric10 evaluations recorded before 2026 report `summary_scores` and
38	#: `element_scores`; the agents have instructed `overall_score` and `elements`
39	#: since. Such a record is not wrong, it is a different vintage — reporting it
40	#: as invalid buries the records that really are.
41	SUPERSEDED_SHAPE_KEYS = ("summary_scores", "element_scores")
42	
43	
44	def classify(eval_data: Dict, schema: Dict) -> Tuple[str, List[str]]:
45	    """Validate, distinguishing a superseded shape from a wrong value.
46	
47	    Returns `("valid" | "superseded" | "invalid", errors)`.
48	
49	    The distinction is the point. All 28 recorded evaluations failed before the
50	    schemas were brought up to the agents (#323), and "Invalid: 28" said nothing
51	    about which were merely old. Of the 20 that still fail, 12 predate the
52	    contract and 8 report `max_points: 84` — a maximum the rubric has never had
53	    (#314). Only the second kind is a defect in a record.
54	    """
55	    errors = []
56	    try:
57	        validate(instance=eval_data, schema=schema)
58	        return "valid", []
59	    except ValidationError as e:
60	        errors.append(f"Validation error: {e.message}")
61	        errors.append(f"  Path: {' -> '.join(str(p) for p in e.path)}")
62	        if e.schema_path:
63	            errors.append(f"  Schema path: {' -> '.join(str(p) for p in e.schema_path)}")
64	        if any(k in eval_data for k in SUPERSEDED_SHAPE_KEYS):
65	            return "superseded", errors
66	        return "invalid", errors
67	
68	
69	def validate_evaluation(eval_data: Dict, schema: Dict) -> Tuple[bool, List[str]]:
70	    """Back-compatible wrapper: superseded records are not valid."""
71	    status, errors = classify(eval_data, schema)
72	    return status == "valid", errors
73	
74	
75	def validate_outputs(paths: List[Path], rubric: str | None = None,
76	                     schema_dir: Path | None = None) -> int:
77	    """Require each explicitly named new output to pass its semantic schema.
78	
79	    Directory names and superseded shapes do not exempt a new output. This
80	    path reads only the files named by the caller, so an evaluator can check
81	    its own output without reading another evaluator's judgements (#833).
82	    """
83	    schema_dir = schema_dir or Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "src/download/prompts"
84	    names = {"rubric10-semantic": "rubric10_semantic_schema.json",
85	             "rubric20-semantic": "rubric20_semantic_schema.json"}
86	    failed = not paths
87	    for path in paths:
88	        try:
89	            doc = load_evaluation(path)
90	            if not isinstance(doc, dict):
91	                raise ValueError("evaluation must be a JSON object")
92	            declared = doc.get("rubric")
93	            if not isinstance(declared, str) or declared not in names:
94	                raise ValueError(f"no semantic evaluation schema for rubric {declared!r}")
95	            if rubric is not None and declared != rubric:
96	                raise ValueError(f"expected {rubric}, found {declared}")
97	            valid, errors = validate_evaluation(doc, load_schema(schema_dir / names[declared]))
98	            if not valid:
99	                raise ValueError("\n".join(errors))
100	        except (OSError, ValueError, jsonschema.SchemaError) as exc:
101	            print(f"INVALID {path}: {exc}")
102	            failed = True
103	        else:
104	            print(f"VALID {path}: {declared}")
105	    return int(failed)
106	
107	
108	#: A directory whose name marks its contents as kept evidence rather than a
109	#: live artifact: an archive, a superseded set, or a dated snapshot of one
110	#: arm's scores. An invalid record in one of these is what an older
111	#: instrument produced and must not be rewritten to satisfy today's schema,
112	#: so it is reported and does not fail the run.
113	KEPT_DIR = _re.compile(r"^(?:_archive|superseded)|^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}(?:[_-]|$)")
114	
115	
116	def is_kept(path: Path, base: Path) -> bool:
117	    """Is any directory between `base` and `path` an archive marker?"""
118	    return any(KEPT_DIR.match(part) for part in path.relative_to(base).parts[:-1])
119	
120	
121	def discover(base: Path) -> List[Path]:
122	    """Every evaluation JSON under `base`, at any depth.
123	
124	    The loop was `{rubric}_semantic/concatenated/*.json` — one directory per
125	    rubric, one level deep (#833). That reached 28 of the 204 semantic
126	    artifacts on disk: not `label_aware/`, which is where every evaluation
127	    since 2026-08 lives and which the cross-arm table reads, not the dated
128	    per-arm subdirectories beside it, and not the archives. The rubric a file
129	    declares decides which schema it is judged against, so the directory does
130	    not have to.
131	    """
132	    return sorted(base.rglob("*_evaluation.json"))
133	
134	
135	def main(eval_base: Path | None = None, schema_dir: Path | None = None) -> int:
136	    """Validate every evaluation JSON under `data/evaluation_llm`.
137	
138	    The two roots are arguments so that the exit code — the thing #833 asked
139	    for, and the thing four tests of the helpers did not reach — can be
140	    exercised end to end over a tree built for the purpose.
141	    """
142	    base_dir = Path(__file__).parent.parent
143	    schema_dir = schema_dir or base_dir / "src" / "download" / "prompts"
144	    eval_base = eval_base or base_dir / "data" / "evaluation_llm"
145	
146	    schemas = {
147	        "rubric10-semantic": load_schema(schema_dir / "rubric10_semantic_schema.json"),
148	        "rubric20-semantic": load_schema(schema_dir / "rubric20_semantic_schema.json"),
149	    }
150	
151	    eval_files = discover(eval_base)
152	    if not eval_files:
153	        print(f"No evaluation files found in {eval_base}")
154	        return 1
155	
156	    print(f"Found {len(eval_files)} evaluation file(s) under {eval_base}\n")
157	
158	    counts = {("live", k): 0 for k in ("valid", "superseded", "invalid", "unreadable")}
159	    counts.update({("kept", k): 0 for k in ("valid", "superseded", "invalid", "unreadable")})
160	    no_schema: Dict[str, int] = {}
161	    live_invalid: List[Tuple[Path, List[str]]] = []
162	    kept_invalid: List[Tuple[Path, List[str]]] = []
163	
164	    for eval_file in eval_files:
165	        where = "kept" if is_kept(eval_file, eval_base) else "live"
166	        shown = eval_file.relative_to(eval_base)
167	        try:
168	            eval_data = load_evaluation(eval_file)
169	            if not isinstance(eval_data, dict):
170	                raise ValueError("evaluation must be a JSON object")
171	        except Exception as e:
172	            print(f"❌ {shown}: failed to load: {e}")
173	            counts[(where, "unreadable")] += 1
174	            continue
175	
176	        rubric = eval_data.get("rubric", "unknown")
177	        if rubric not in schemas:
178	            # Named and counted, not skipped in silence: the presence-style
179	            # rubric10/rubric20 outputs have no schema in this repository, and
180	            # a reader of the summary should see that they were not judged.
181	            no_schema[str(rubric)] = no_schema.get(str(rubric), 0) + 1
182	            continue
183	
184	        status, errors = classify(eval_data, schemas[rubric])
185	        counts[(where, status)] += 1
186	        if status == "invalid":
187	            (kept_invalid if where == "kept" else live_invalid).append((shown, errors))
188	        elif status == "superseded":
189	            print(f"🕐 {shown}: superseded shape — {errors[0]}")
190	
191	    for label, rows in (("live", live_invalid), ("kept as evidence", kept_invalid)):
192	        for shown, errors in rows:
193	            print(f"❌ {shown} ({label}):")
194	            for error in errors:
195	                print(f"     {error}")
196	
197	    print()
198	    print("=" * 60)
199	    print("SUMMARY (judged against a schema):")
200	    for where in ("live", "kept"):
201	        row = {k: counts[(where, k)] for k in ("valid", "superseded", "invalid", "unreadable")}
202	        print(f"  {where:5}  valid {row['valid']:4}  superseded {row['superseded']:3}  "
203	              f"invalid {row['invalid']:3}  unreadable {row['unreadable']:3}")
204	    if no_schema:
205	        print("  no schema in this repository, not judged: "
206	              + ", ".join(f"{k} {v}" for k, v in sorted(no_schema.items())))
207	    print("=" * 60)
208	
209	    # A superseded record is historical output of a contract that no longer
210	    # applies, and one kept under an archive marker is evidence of what an
211	    # older instrument produced: reported, never rewritten to pass. Only a
212	    # live invalid artifact fails the run.
213	    return 0 if not live_invalid and not counts[("live", "unreadable")] else 1
214	
215	
216	def cli(argv: List[str] | None = None) -> int:
